en: The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Deliverance from Suffering and Calamity, translated by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Great Tang, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavān was staying at Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove.
At the Jetavana Grove,
together with an immeasurable number of śrāvakas, bodhisattvas mahāsattvas,
as well as devas, humans, asuras, and others.
He was surrounded before and behind by an immeasurable great assembly.
At that time, within the assembly,
there was a bodhisattva named Inexpressible Adornment of Merit.
Rising from his seat, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet,
joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One, there are now immeasurable sentient beings in this world.”
Due to the causes and conditions of afflictions,
one creates various evil karmas and shall fall into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, or animals; or else,
among gods and humans, one will undergo various forms of intense suffering.
"I only pray that you will take pity on us and deliver us through skillful means.
The Buddha said, "Good man, excellent, excellent!
It is well that you, out of compassion for all sentient beings, have made such a request."
Listen attentively, listen attentively!
I shall now briefly explain for you the skillful means for uprooting and delivering all sufferings.
Noble son, there is a Buddha, a World-Honored One.
He is named the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Acala.
For the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings,
he has taught this dhāraṇī so that the multitude may recite and keep it in mind.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:

*kakkani kakkani | luñcani luñcani | dhurucchanī dhurucchanī | trāsani trāsani | pratyahan pratyahana | sarvakarmapraśamanapramardane svāhā*. If there be any son of good family or daughter of good family...
With utmost sincerity and reverence, one should pay homage to the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha Acalanātha, and uphold this dhāraṇī.
All previously committed five ānantarya karmas, the four grave offenses, and the ten evil deeds [shall be purified].
All the karmic offenses of disparaging the noble sages and slandering the True Dharma shall be completely extinguished.
At the time of death,
that Buddha Akṣobhya, together with various bodhisattvas, will appear before them.
He praised and comforted him, causing him to rejoice, and further addressed him, saying:
"I have now come to welcome you; you should follow me to the Buddha-land from which I have come."
After his life has ended,
he will certainly be reborn in the pure buddha-field of the Tathāgata Acala.
Furthermore, son of good family, there is another Blessed One.
Named the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha King Who Extirpates Evil Destinies,
for the sake of benefiting and bringing happiness to all sentient beings,
he has taught this dhāraṇī so that the multitude may recite and contemplate it.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:
*sudati sudati sarvabhāvaviśuddhe śodhani viśodhani sarvakarma-viśodhani svāhā*. If there be any son of good family or daughter of good family...
By reverently making offerings with utmost sincerity to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha King Who Extinguishes Evil Destinies and upholding this mantra,
one shall constantly remember past lives for fourteen thousand kalpas and obtain a male body in every place of rebirth.
He was endowed with all the sense faculties and possessed deep faith in cause and effect.
He was skilled in various arts and crafts, had a profound understanding of all treatises,
delighted in practicing generosity, and felt weary of and renounced all sensual desires.
By not committing evil karma, one is free from all perils and fears;
possessing the wisdom of right livelihood, one is loved and respected by all;
constantly associating with virtuous friends, one perpetually hears the true Dharma.
He never for a moment abandoned the aspiration for bodhicitta;
he adorned himself with all manner of virtues,
maintained excellent discipline, and feared all evil deeds.
They shall never suffer from lack, remaining ever-disciplined, gentle, and fond of tranquility;
they will constantly experience happiness among gods and humans,
and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
They never regress from the ten pāramitās;
they constantly aspire to bring benefit and happiness to all sentient beings,
and their various practices are not solely for their own benefit.
In whatever place they are born, they shall always behold the Buddha,
uphold the True Dharma, and join the assembly of noble sages.
When the Bhagavān had finished speaking this sutra, [the assembly rejoiced].
The śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, and all the devas, humans, asuras, and others,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken,
were all greatly filled with joy.
Believing, accepting, and practicing accordingly.
The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Deliverance from Suffering and Calamity.
